title: [Autour de La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois, pages 1 à 67] : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (continued from the previous page). S is a henselian trait with generic point η and residue field k. Here k is Q or a number field, so the residue characteristic is 0. U_η is a curve of type (g,ν) over η; the running example is (g,ν)=(1,1), a once-punctured elliptic curve. Two exact sequences are in play:
- (30) 1 → T → E_η → E_k → 1. Here T is the inertia group. Since the residue characteristic is 0, T ≅ \hat{Z}(1).
- (31) 1 → π → E_{U_η} → E_η → 1. Here π = π_1 of the geometric generic fibre.

On the previous page Grothendieck notes that the outer action of T on π is non-trivial in the bad-reduction case. So E_k does not act outer-ly on π in any canonical way.

This page. Choose a splitting s: E_k → E_η of (30); in characteristic 0 such splittings correspond to compatible systems of roots of a uniformizer. Pulling (31) back along s gives an extension of E_k by π, hence an outer Galois action of E_k on π.

Question 1: is this extension 'admissible', i.e. does it come from an algebraic curve over k (or a finite extension of k)? Grothendieck's answer is 'Sans doute pas'. Which curves could it be, if one wants 'reduced' curves of type (g,ν)? These do not exist: the special fibre is a stable curve, not a smooth curve of type (g,ν). The marginal note seems to add that there are nevertheless 'reduced' combinatorial or arithmetic types attached to π.

Question 2: given a section of (30) and one of (31), so that E_k genuinely acts on π (not just outer-ly), what should one expect of such an action? Suggested approach: 'la structure à l'∞ des variétés modulaires de Teichmüller'. That is, the boundary of the (Deligne–Mumford compactified) moduli stacks M_{g,ν}, with degenerate curves seen as points at infinity of the Teichmüller tower.

Then comes a 'Conjecture-à-tout-hasard', continued on the next page, listing conditions claimed to be equivalent:
- (a) U_η has good reduction over S.
- (b) The outer action of T on π is trivial. Equivalently, any splitting of (31), e.g. one given by a rational point, induces a homomorphism T → π.
- (c) T acts trivially on π^ab = H_1(U_η̄).
- (d) The same for H_1 with T_ℓ coefficients, ℓ prime to the residue characteristic; for ℓ = p one would use p-divisible groups.
- (e) For k of finite type over Q, the extension of E_k by π defined via a section of (30) is admissible, i.e. comes from an algebraic curve over k or a finite extension.
- (f) The E_k-action obtained from sections of (30) and (31) is 'not too crazy', a notion still to be defined.

Purpose: understanding the degeneration and boundary behaviour of the Galois action on π_1 of curves, as an input to the anabelian programme and to the Galois action on the Teichmüller tower (Longue Marche, 1981).
errors: (a) ⇔ (c)/(d) is false in general. Triviality of inertia on H_1 (ℓ-adic) is equivalent, by Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich, to good reduction of the Jacobian. That only gives stable reduction of compact type (tree-like dual graph), not good reduction of the curve. Example: a genus-2 curve degenerating to two elliptic curves meeting at a point.

For affine curves (ν > 0), (c) fails even more clearly. Example: P^1 minus {0,1,∞,λ} with λ specialising to 0. Inertia acts trivially on H_1, which is spanned by cusp loops of weight -2, yet the 4-pointed curve has bad reduction. Abelian data cannot detect it; one needs at least a metabelian or higher nilpotent quotient of π. The equivalence (a)⇔(c) does hold in the running example (1,1), since there the only stable degeneration is the nodal cubic, which is not of compact type.
(a) ⇔ (b) is correct. It was later proved by T. Oda (proper curves, pro-ℓ) and A. Tamagawa (hyperbolic, possibly affine curves).

On 'Sans doute pas' (non-admissibility): a weight argument confirms it. The G_k-action obtained from a splitting acts on H_1 with weights 0 and -2 in the bad-reduction case (e.g. a Tate curve: 0 ⊕ Z_ℓ(1)). A smooth proper curve over a number field has pure weight -1, so the action cannot be geometric in the naive sense. Grothendieck leaves this unproved on the page.

ideas.what: Outer Galois action of E_k on π obtained from a splitting of the inertia sequence of a henselian trait; question whether it is of geometric origin
ideas.modern_name: Galois action at tangential base points / limit action at a boundary point of M_{g,n}; Galois action on π_1 of stable (degenerate) curves
ideas.usually_credited_to: Deligne (tangential base points, 1989); Ihara–Nakamura (1997, maximally degenerate curves); Nakamura, Asada
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984) discusses tangential base points and points at infinity of the Teichmüller tower in general terms; this specific question is not known to me in published form

ideas.what: Study the Galois action via the structure at infinity of the Teichmüller modular varieties
ideas.modern_name: Boundary of Deligne–Mumford M̄_{g,n}; Grothendieck–Teichmüller theory via degeneration / Knudsen–Mumford gluing
ideas.usually_credited_to: Grothendieck (Esquisse), developed by Ihara, Nakamura, Drinfeld, Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme §2–3; La Longue Marche (1981)

ideas.what: Good reduction ⇔ inertia acts trivially (outer) on the geometric π_1 of the curve
ideas.modern_name: Oda's good reduction criterion for curves (anabelian Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich)
ideas.usually_credited_to: T. Oda (1990/1995); A. Tamagawa (1997, affine/hyperbolic case)
ideas.where_published: Possibly in La Longue Marche itself; not in Esquisse as far as I know

ideas.what: Equivalence with triviality on H_1 / T_ℓ, and a p-adic version via p-divisible groups
ideas.modern_name: Néron–Ogg–Shafarevich criterion; Grothendieck's p-divisible group / Fontaine-style crystalline criterion
ideas.usually_credited_to: Serre–Tate (1968), Grothendieck (SGA 7 for semistable), Coleman–Iovita / Fontaine for p-adic
ideas.where_published: SGA 7 I (Exp. IX) for abelian varieties

ideas.what: Conjectural criterion: good reduction ⇔ the E_k-action obtained from splittings is admissible (geometric) or 'not too crazy'
ideas.modern_name: Geometricity of Galois sections/actions in degenerating families (no exact modern counterpart)

missed.claim: Grothendieck explicitly conjectures, around 1981, that good reduction of a curve over a henselian trait is equivalent to trivial outer inertia action on its geometric fundamental group. This is Oda's theorem (≈1990), later extended by Tamagawa. The Grothendieck priority/motivation is not usually cited.
missed.quote: Conjecture-à-tout-hasard : Les conditions suivantes sont équivalentes a) Il y a bonne réduction sur S b) L'action extérieure de T sur π est triviale
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a historical-credit point: the anabelian good-reduction criterion appears as an explicit Grothendieck conjecture predating Oda.

missed.claim: Clauses (e)/(f): characterising good reduction by 'admissibility' (geometric origin) of the E_k-action induced by splittings of the inertia sequence, and the vague 'not too crazy' condition. No standard theorem matches this. A natural modern formulation would compare such actions with Galois actions at tangential base points on the boundary of M̄_{g,ν}, e.g. weight or graph-of-groups characterisations.
missed.quote: est-elle “admissible” ?, i.e. définie par une courbe algébrique ? Sans doute pas
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is a precise question about which E_k-actions on π come from degenerations. It relates to the classification of Galois actions on π_1 of stable curves (Nakamura, Ihara–Nakamura, Hoshi–Mochizuki combinatorial anabelian geometry).

deep.surprise_reason: The page contains an explicit, dated (~1981) Grothendieck conjecture equal to the later Oda/Tamagawa good-reduction criterion, plus an unexplored 'admissibility' variant. The abelian clauses (c)/(d) are wrong in general, and the core idea is now a known theorem, so the interest is mainly historical priority.
transcription_corrections: 'E_h' throughout is almost certainly 'E_k' (k = residue field, as on the previous page).
'(inexistant !)' likely 'inexistantes !' referring to the reduced curves.
'qui comprend une affectation de une action' is probably 'qui permettent de définir une action de E_k sur π' (the next page uses this phrasing: 'permettant de faire opérer E_k sur π').

'[-Sans-] S'y attendre[?], une voie à tâter une[?] par la structure : l'∞ des variétés modulaires' is better read as '…, une voie à tâter serait par la structure à l'∞ des variétés modulaires de Teichmüller !'.
The marginal note likely reads 'mais il y a types (combinatoires/arithmétiques) “réduits” de π …'; it remains uncertain.
